How do I get a free key? (2 minutes)

Google AI Studio is free, takes about two minutes, and doesn't ask for a credit card. It's the one to pick: the chat sends your whole list every time you ask something, and this is the free key with room for that.

1
Tap aistudio.google.com/apikey to open AI Studio.
2
Sign in with your Google account. Accept the terms if it asks — it lands you on the API keys page.
3
Tap Create API key. If it asks for a project, take the one it offers.
4
Copy it. It starts with AIza. You can come back and copy it again later, so there's no rush.
5
Come back here, paste it in the box above, tap Save. Done.

Prefer somewhere else? console.groq.com (gsk_) is free and much faster to answer, but its free allowance is measured in words per minute rather than questions per day, so a long conversation about a big list runs into it. openrouter.ai (sk-or-) is free too, and paid Claude keys (sk-ant-) work. The app recognises which is which on its own.

Import from AniList / MyAnimeList

Already have a list elsewhere? Pull it in — covers, status and progress and all.

Your list must be public. Both your watch and reading lists come over.

or paste it

Paste your list from Notes, messages, or anywhere — one title per line, as messy as you like. After previewing, tap a status on each title (or use Set all). "Title | status | ep 5 | ★4" style lines are understood too.

How it works

Everything you watch and read, in one place — with covers, air times and progress filled in for you.

Add anything
Tap + and type a title. Autofill pulls the real cover, episode count, genres and watch order — anime, TV, movies, manga, manhwa and webtoons. No setup, no API key.
Your list is backed up — save the code
Backup is already on. What you need from it is the sync code: it's the only thing that restores your list on a new phone, or after clearing your browser data. Save it somewhere you'll still have it if this device doesn't survive. You can turn backup off if you'd rather the list never left the device.
Watch or Read
The switch beside the search box flips between your watch list and your reading list. They're kept completely separate.
Never miss an episode
The calendar shows what airs this week for the shows you follow, in your own time zone — and it tracks delays. Turn on the bell to get a notification the moment one drops.
Find your next one
The compass suggests titles you don't have yet, picked from what you already watch — real community recommendations, not guesses.
Watch it your way
Open any show and you get every episode, with artwork — tap one to jump there, and your progress follows. Watch somewhere we don't list? Open Sources, start any episode on your site, and paste that page's address. That one link is the whole setup: no key, no second step. If a show ever opens on the wrong page, tap Set the right one and paste the correct address — WatchList remembers what that site calls it, for good.
Your progress keeps itself
You don't have to press anything. Use the site's own next-episode link and WatchList follows you — it banks the one you finished and moves to the next, and you'll see the number change at the top. Same when you're reading. If it ever gets one wrong, the bar that appears says Undo and puts it straight back.
Make it yours
The palette repaints the whole app — Naruto orange, Sasuke purple, Zoro green and more. Or build your own: pick any two colours and tap Harmonize — it keeps your colours, turns them into a palette that actually works, sets the glow and brightness to match, and names it. Each title also quietly borrows its own artwork's colour as you browse.
Ask it things (optional)
There's a chat that knows your list — what to watch next, what's short tonight, what fits your mood. It needs a free key (about two minutes, no card); Settings → AI walks you through it step by step. Everything else works without one.
Hand your setup to a friend
Got your site working? Sources → Share mine gives you a link. Whoever opens it sees plainly what they're getting and taps Accept — and they get everything: your site, the links you taught it, and every show you corrected by hand. It never changes your own settings, and they don't need to be your friend in the app.
Watch together, properly
In a watch party the host presses play and everyone starts together — on their own copy, in full quality, with their own audio. Nothing is streamed between you, so nothing looks compressed and nobody's battery suffers. The host's pause and skip carry across too. There's voice and video alongside it, with each person in their own colour.
Lock it (optional)
A password encrypts your whole list — unreadable without it, here and in the cloud. You'll get a one-time recovery key; it's the only way back in if you forget the password. Save both. Lose both and the list is gone for good — there's no backdoor. You can also unlock with Face ID or your fingerprint instead of typing — whatever your device supports.
